payload.title: LimitedCounter: design a class

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the complete LimitedCounter class, including the constructor and any required instance variables and methods. A LimitedCounter accepts increments until a limit that is given to the constructor is reached. increment adds one to the counter and returns true if the limit has not been reached, and returns false (without changing the counter) otherwise. reset sets the counter back to its starting value. remaining returns the number of increments still allowed. Examples of the behavior are listed in the following table.

| Statement | Result |
|---|---|
| LimitedCounter c = new LimitedCounter(5); | creates a counter that accepts at most 5 increments |
| c.increment() (called 5 times) | true each time |
| c.increment() | false (the limit has been reached) |
| c.remaining() | 0 |
| c.reset(); c.remaining() | 5 |

payload.stem: A school district records how long each student spends on each page of its online homework portal. The district plans to give this data, labeled with student names, to a private company that builds study-habit apps. Which of the following is the most significant privacy concern with this plan?

options.text: The data is useful only if every student spends exactly the same amount of time on every page.
options.why: This is not a privacy concern; data about differences between students is exactly what makes such data informative.

options.text: The data could be used to profile individual students, and to share information about them, without their knowledge or consent.
options.why: The data identifies each student and describes their behavior, so giving it to a third party can expose personal information the students never agreed to share.

options.text: Data collected by a school district automatically becomes public domain, so anyone may copy it.
options.why: Collecting data does not make it public domain; the concern is who may access the data and for what purpose.

options.text: Recording page times makes the portal load too slowly for students to finish their homework.
options.why: This is a performance concern, not a privacy concern.

student_thinking: Identify what personal information the program collects

payload.stem: A company writes a program that screens job applications. The program learns its rules from the applications of employees the company hired during the past ten years, and nearly all of those employees graduated from the same few universities. Which of the following is the most likely effect of this design?

options.text: The program will treat all applicants fairly because a computer has no opinions of its own.
options.why: A program inherits patterns from the data it learns from, so it can repeat past unfairness; being a computer does not make it neutral.

options.text: The program will run correctly only on computers made by the same company that wrote it.
options.why: The fairness of the screening does not depend on the manufacturer of the computer.

options.text: The program may favor applicants from those universities and unfairly screen out qualified applicants from other backgrounds.
options.why: The program learned from a narrow, historical set of hires, so its rules can reproduce that bias and affect which applicants are considered.

options.text: The program will become more accurate over time no matter what data it is given.
options.why: Accuracy depends on the quality and variety of the data; biased data does not produce unbiased results.
